newsitem.title: CHINA: China yuan interbank market trade down in November.
newsitem.headline: China yuan interbank market trade down in November.

text.p: China's Shanghai-based renminbi interbank lending market traded 56.2 billion yuan in November, a daily turnover of 2.7 billion, down 931 million from October, the Shanghai Securities News said on Wednesday.

The rates for most of the seven contracts traded on the market went up in November, with only the 20-day contract falling a little, the newspaper said. Other contracts are for one day, seven, 30, 60, 90 and 120 days.
The seven-day contract was the most active, with volume of the 30-day contract rising the most, by 72.9 percent, it said.

Shanghai traders said banks and other financial institutions had much of their money involved in underwriting the nation's first seven-year treasury bonds issued from November 1 to 20, causing volume on the market to fall.
The rates for most contracts dropped sharply in September and October because of a bank interest rate cut in late August and rose in November on a technical rebound, they said.
